subject: Question about nested logit model in mirt

messages.author: 0a2f118b18e6b12c
messages.subject: Question about nested logit model in mirt
parts:
Dear Dr. Chalmers,
I'm running the nested logit model in mirt for a project, and I have little questions I need your help with. 
In the mirt package description (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mirt/mirt.pdf), page 176,  under the simdata function, itemtype says that "For nested logit models the ’correct’ category is always the lowest category (i.e., == 1)". So when we simulate response data using itemtype=nestlogit, the default is that the lowest category is zero and this category of zero is the correct answer (unless we define mins=1)
However, the example (p.180-181) says key=c(NA,NA,NA,1). I'm wondering if the key should be c(NA,NA,NA,0) because the item was simulated under the nested logit model using defaults.
When I ran the example code as it was (set.seed(201187)), the results are below:

$Item_4
          a1            d   g u  ak0  ak1      ak2  d0    d1      d2
par -0.903 -2.466 0 1   0 -0.477 -0.318  0 -2.622 -1.77

The discrimination parameter a1 is negative, which is odd because it is simulated from rlnorm(4,0,.2). I changed the key=c(NA,NA,NA,0) and the discrimination for the item simulated under the nested logit model is still negative. Changing the random seed did not help either. 
So I'm wondering if I misunderstood something about the answer key and the negative discrimination. I'm using mirt 1.29. I tried the code in mirt 1.33.2 but the results stayed the same.
Thank you very much and I look forward to your reply. 
Happy new year!!!
Best wishes,
Hoan Do.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Question about nested logit model in mirt
parts:
Hi Hoan Do,

Indeed, that was a mistake in the example code. Thanks for pointing this out; I've made changes to this example that will appear on the next release. Cheers.

Phil
